acme_ops (Acme): Hey team — after we applied the pin to our model for production traffic, a subset of embeddings responses are suddenly 2048-d, while most are 1536-d. Happening intermittently across requests. Example request id: req_0a9f. Can someone help?

jess (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a raw request/response snippet (headers + small response) and confirm which model string you're passing in the request body?

acme_ops (Acme): Curl we used:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1b-pinned","input":"test item"}'```
Response example (trimmed):```json
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.01,0.02,...(2048 values)...]}],"model":"rwd-embed-1b-2026-02-09"}```
And error we see in our app: "embedding length 2048 != expected 1536". We pinned to rwd-embed-1b@2025-11-17 (confirmed in Console).

eli (infra): Thanks — two quick questions: 1) when you say "pinned" did you pin the canonical model id or a variant alias? 2) any canary/burst routing enabled on your account? Looks like some requests are routed to a variant that has a different output dim.

acme_ops (Acme): We used the Console pin UI and it shows a pin for rwd-embed-1b -> v2025-11-17 (UI shows locked). No deliberate canary.

anika (eng-ml): Flagging what I've seen in a related roll: a quantized build accidentally changed the final projection size during a variant build, so model binary produced 2048-d vectors. There was a bug in the compatibility guard that allowed variant substitution for pinned customers when a capacity fallback occurred. Possible explanation: some requests hit the quantized variant.

jess (support): That matches the symptom. Quick mitigation: 1) in your request set the exact model identifier (the Console shows the full model id string) rather than the alias; 2) we can temporarily unpin + re-pin the older build or pin to a specific sha to force exact binary. Will that work for you?

acme_ops (Acme): We can try explicit model id. Any exact param name we should use?

eli (infra): Use the exact model id field, e.g. "model":"rwd-embed-1b:sha256:abcdef123456" or the date-qualified id like "rwd-embed-1b@2025-11-17" (Console shows both). That bypasses alias/variant routing. Also check headers — avoid any X-RW-Beta routing header.

anika (eng-ml): From our side we'll open an internal ticket to patch the compatibility check and make pinned mappings strict. Repro notes for ENG: reproduce by setting pin to alias and then launching a quantized variant with a different output dim; simulate capacity fallback to variant and confirm mixed dim outputs.

deploy-bot: Created issue RW-ENG-4821: "Pinned model alias allowed variant substitution -> embedding dim mismatch" and assigned to eng-ml.

tickets-bot: INC-2345 opened for customer-facing escalation. Priority P1.

jess (support): ETA: eng-ml says a hotfix to the compatibility guard is targeted within 24 hours; we'll confirm when deployed. Temporary remediation steps: 1) set explicit model id in your requests, 2) if you prefer we can unpin and re-pin to a known-good sha on your behalf. Which do you prefer?

acme_ops (Acme): Please unpin and re-pin to the previous sha for now — that minimizes dev churn. Also please confirm when the hotfix is live so we can remove our workaround. Thanks! :pray: 

eli (infra): Doing the unpin/re-pin now and will DM you the pinned sha. I'll also check routing logs for any requests from your project hitting the quantized nodes and forward them to you.

anika (eng-ml): Noted — we'll post status updates to INC-2345 and add the postmortem details when done.

jess (support): Closing loop — we'll update this thread and INC-2345. Thanks for the quick repro info, that made triage fast. :thumbsup:
